knowledge:
- key_parameters: q=The order of the partial correlation (dimension of the potential separator) used to control for confounding variables ;; clusterSize=An integer specifying the number of processors to use for parallel execution via snow and rlecuyer ;; pairup.i=A vector of indices or names representing the first set of variables (e.g., transcription factors) to restrict pairwise calculations ;; pairup.j=A vector of indices or names representing the second set of variables (e.g., target genes) to restrict pairwise calculations ;; threshold=A numeric cutoff value for non-rejection rates or association scores above/below which edges are removed ;; topPairs=An integer specifying the exact number of top-scoring interactions to retain in the inferred network ;; qOrders=A vector of specific q-orders to use when calculating average non-rejection rates
- alternatives: qpPCC=Computes Pearson correlation coefficients, which is faster but cannot distinguish direct from indirect interactions ;; qpUnifRndAssociation=Generates uniform random association values to serve as a baseline control ;; Other methods mentioned include graphical lasso (glasso), shrinkage covariance estimation, and Bayesian sparse graphical models
- when_to_use: Use this package when you need to reconstruct undirected gene expression networks or eQTL networks from high-throughput datasets where the number of features (p) is much larger than the number of samples (n)
- pitfalls: Specifying a single q-order in qpNrr requires an educated guess and can affect statistical power; using qpAvgNrr is more stable but may have lower power for identifying disconnected pairs mediated by many intermediate vertices. Full-order partial correlations cannot be computed when n < p because the sample covariance matrix is non-invertible. Functional coherence estimation is highly dependent on the availability and quality of GO annotations for the target organism.

workflows.name: eqtl_network_estimation
workflows.intent: Estimate an eQTL network from genotyping cross data, physical maps, and gene annotations.
input: cross.RData (a qtl cross object containing genotypes and phenotypes/expression)
physical_map.RData (a physical map list of marker positions)
gene_annotation.csv (a data frame containing genomic coordinates of genes)
genome_info.RData (a Seqinfo object containing chromosome lengths)
workflows.stages: 1. Define estimation parameters using eQTLnetworkEstimationParam ;; 2. Estimate the initial network using eQTLnetworkEstimate with a formula ;; 3. Apply FDR correction to filter the network ;; 4. Refine the network using non-rejection rates conditioning on genes ;; 5. Filter by effect size (epsilon) and select significant associations (alpha) ;; 6. Extract eQTL associations using alleQTL ;; 7. Plot the network using hive plots or standard graphs
workflows.code:
param <- eQTLnetworkEstimationParam(cross, physicalMap=pMap,
                                    geneAnnotation=annot, genome=genome)
eqtlnet.q0 <- eQTLnetworkEstimate(param, ~ marker + gene, verbose=FALSE)
eqtlnet.q0.fdr <- eQTLnetworkEstimate(param, estimate=eqtlnet.q0,
                                      p.value=0.05, method="fdr")
eqtlnet.q0.fdr.nrr <- eQTLnetworkEstimate(param, ~ marker + gene | gene(q=3),
                                          estimate=eqtlnet.q0.fdr, verbose=FALSE)
eqtlnet.q0.fdr.nrr <- eQTLnetworkEstimate(param, estimate=eqtlnet.q0.fdr.nrr,
                                          epsilon=0.1)
eqtls <- alleQTL(eqtlnet.q0.fdr.nrr)
eqtlnet.q0.fdr.nrr.sel <- eQTLnetworkEstimate(param, estimate=eqtlnet.q0.fdr.nrr,
                                              alpha=0.05)
plot(eqtlnet.q0.fdr.nrr.sel, type="hive", chr=chr)

workflows.name: transcriptional_regulatory_network_inference
workflows.intent: Infer a transcriptional regulatory network from gene expression data, optionally restricting to transcription factors and validating against a gold standard.
input: expression_data.RData (an ExpressionSet object containing gene expression data)
gold_standard.csv (optional data frame of known TF-target interactions for validation)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate Pearson correlation coefficients using qpPCC or average non-rejection rates using qpAvgNrr ;; 2. Calculate precision-recall curves against a gold standard using qpPrecisionRecall ;; 3. Determine a score threshold for a desired precision/recall level using qpPRscoreThreshold ;; 4. Reconstruct the network graph using qpGraph or qpAnyGraph ;; 5. Estimate functional coherence of the network modules using qpFunctionalCoherence ;; 6. Extract top pairs using qpTopPairs and plot the network using qpPlotNetwork
workflows.code:
pcc.estimates <- qpPCC(subset.gds680.eset)
avgnrr.estimates <- qpAvgNrr(subset.gds680.eset,
                             pairup.i=largestIQRgenesO2netTFs,
                             pairup.j=largestIQRgenesO2net, verbose=FALSE)
pcc.prerec <- qpPrecisionRecall(abs(pcc.estimates$R), subset.filtered.regulon6.1.I,
                                decreasing=TRUE, pairup.i=largestIQRgenesO2netTFs,
                                pairup.j=largestIQRgenesO2net,
                                recallSteps=c(seq(0,0.1,0.01),seq(0.2,1,0.1)))
avgnrr.prerec <- qpPrecisionRecall(avgnrr.estimates, subset.filtered.regulon6.1.I,
                                   decreasing=FALSE,
                                   recallSteps=c(seq(0,0.1,0.01),seq(0.2,1,0.1)))
thr <- qpPRscoreThreshold(avgnrr.prerec, level=0.5, recall.level=FALSE, max.score=0)
g <- qpGraph(avgnrr.estimates, threshold=thr, return.type="graphNEL")
qpCliqueNumber(g, verbose=FALSE)
pac.estimates <- qpPAC(subset.gds680.eset, g, verbose=FALSE)
qpg50preFC <- qpFunctionalCoherence(qpg50pre,
                   TFgenes=regulonTFgenes,
                   chip="org.EcK12.eg.db",
                   minRMsize=5, clusterSize=8)
qpPlotNetwork(g, pairup.i=largestIQRgenesO2netTFs, pairup.j=largestIQRgenesO2net,
              annotation="org.EcK12.eg.db")
